name: Tibial Shaft Fracture
definition: Fracture of the tibial diaphysis, often high-energy and at risk of open injury, compartment syndrome, infection and delayed union.

investigations.principle: Urgent radiographs define pattern; open injuries need trauma pathway.
investigations.MRI: CT for articular extension; MRI is not routine acute shaft fracture.
investigations.radiographs: AP/lateral tibia including knee and ankle.

amber: Repeated neurovascular/compartment checks are essential; do not delay fasciotomy when compartment syndrome is suspected.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Bhagna principles may support later rehabilitation, not substitute for urgent fracture and wound management.

patientEducation.summary: Fracture of the tibial diaphysis, often high-energy and at risk of open injury, compartment syndrome, infection and delayed union.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, breathing/swallowing difficulty, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
